analysis.title: "Long And Wrong": Hedge Funds Puke $6.6 Billion In Brent As The Midterms Gut Oil's War Premium
key_insights: Brent fell from $118 (January contract, Oct 30) to just under $98 at the close of the week ending Nov 6. That is the steepest weekly drop since April 2020 and, per Reuters/LSEG data, the biggest in dollar terms back to 1988.

Per Goldman's Quinn, using CFTC Commitment of Traders data, Managed Money sold $6.6bn of Brent from Oct 27 to Nov 3 alongside a 5.3% price drop. Selling above $6bn has happened only 7 times in 5 years. Liquidation of longs ($4.9bn) was the main driver, and new shorts were a minor part.

The COT window closed Nov 3, so the $6.6bn excludes the 8.7% Brent drop on Wed Nov 4 after the Democratic midterm sweep. Open interest shed $2.7bn that day. The next COT print will show the larger liquidation.
Managed Money net length was rebuilt to about $28bn in October and was around $19bn by Nov 4 (read off a chart, approximate). In April the same cohort was above $45bn net long.

Goldman's CTA framework showed short-term momentum turning negative for the first time since August, unlocking more selling. Medium- and long-term signals are still positive but falling. Per a Market Ear chart cited in the note, CTA downside convexity in oil is large and much of the systematic selling may not yet have been executed.

Goldman's systematic strategies desk said trend-following underperformed in early November as bonds rallied, equities sold off and oil fell. Its fixed-vol trend strategy was down 5.14% month-to-date through Nov 5, after petroleum products were the biggest long signals at end-October.

Historical read: since Liberation Day there were 3 similar episodes of heavy Managed Money Brent selling, and in each, negative flows persisted for the following 2 weeks. The clearest case was after the Iran-US MOU in June 2026.

Counterexample: May 28 to Jun 4, 2024, hedge funds sold $7.9bn of Brent when OPEC scheduled the end of its voluntary output curbs. OPEC then pushed back on the market reaction and Managed Money net length was fully restored.
Options signal a possible exhaustion of selling: Brent recouped 3.9% on Nov 5-6, 3-month implied vol rose, 25-delta put-call skew cheapened, and calls were repurchased.

UBS's Dominic Ellis argues fundamentals still provide a floor, citing a near-700 million barrel drawdown in global inventories. He says the market has spent seven months pricing de-escalation ahead of evidence.

Physical market is mixed: Gulf barrels are returning, and Dubai moved into contango for the first time since July. Per Reuters/UKMTO, attacks on oil-carrying ships are near record pace, and Iran says Hormuz stays shut until the US meets seven conditions.
Goldman's Rich Privorotsky notes gold has traded as an inverse oil trade, up more than 3% on the day Brent fell sharply.

On Friday Nov 6, Trump spoke with Qatar's Emir about a 'comprehensive agreement to end the regional crisis'. The White House then confirmed minor strikes on Iranian air defenses on Qeshm Island, the first ordered action since the election. The article sides with call buyers and expects the war premium to be priced back in.

sector_views.rationale: The article (ZeroHedge's own view) sides with call buyers. Positioning has been cleared out, options show call buying, and de-escalation has been priced in too early for seven months.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning has been cleaned out, calls are being repurchased, implied vol is rising and skew has cheapened. UBS says the 700 million barrel inventory drawdown puts a floor under prices, and a weekend strike on Iranian air defenses resembles the 2024 policymaker pushback that restored net length.
tension_points.bear_case: Following the June 2026 MOU, 3 similar heavy-selling episodes saw 2 more weeks of negative flows. CTA selling may not be fully executed, short-term momentum has turned negative, Gulf barrels are returning and Dubai is in contango.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Two more weeks of grinding liquidation, as after the June 2026 MOU, rather than net length being restored as in 2024.
